title: Iterative learning guides discovery of a cobalt-doped nitride battery catalyst
summary: Iteratively updated regression models screened transition-metal compositions and guided synthesis of three candidate battery catalysts. Cobalt-doped molybdenum nitride, Co 0.1 Mo 0.9 N, showed the best reported performance of these candidates in laboratory lithium-carbon-dioxide and lithium-air cells. Reported low overpotentials were measured at 50 milliamperes per gram; they do not establish commercial cell performance or broad model accuracy.
ai_technology: Iterative supervised regression; random forest; Gaussian-process regression; XGBoost; nearest-neighbor regression
organization: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China; Zhejiang University

evidence.tested: Three selected catalyst compositions were synthesized and characterized; Co 0.1 Mo 0.9 N was evaluated against MoN and carbon-nanotube cathode comparators in laboratory battery tests.
evidence.unknown: Generalization is not established by the reported 0.106-volt mean absolute error on only three selected candidates. Practical battery durability, manufacturing and device-level benefit are unestablished; reported overpotential depends on current density and cell conditions.
evidence.ai_role: Regression models learned catalyst-descriptor/overpotential relationships, with measurements added across five iterations before screening 15012 compositions and selecting three for synthesis.

source_review.scope: Primary publisher article-front metadata and abstract, complete official author supporting information Methods/model tables/experimental characterizations and result captions, and current PubMed notice metadata. Paywalled main article body was not read; no independent replication performed.
